decisions.mark: explains that the health monitor does NOT invoke its status callback from the monitor thread — it queues events under a mutex and the caller drains them on its own thread
decisions.detail: QUOTE: **Swap-then-run.** `HealthMonitor::process_events` swaps the queue out under `event_mutex_`, then runs callbacks outside the lock, on the engine thread. | WHY: The answer states that the monitor queues events under event_mutex_ and process_events drains them and runs callbacks on the engine (caller) thread, not the monitor thread. || QUOTE: Swap-then-run. `HealthMonitor::process_events` swaps the queue out under `event_mutex_`, then runs callbacks outside the lock, on the engine thread. | WHY: The answer says events are queued under `event_mutex_` and that `process_events` runs the callbacks on the engine thread, not on the monitor thread. That covers the queue, the mutex and the caller-side drain. || QUOTE: **Swap-then-run.** `HealthMonitor::process_events` swaps the queue out under `event_mutex_`, then runs callbacks outside the lock, on the engine thread. | WHY: The answer states that the monitor thread queues events under event_mutex_ and process_events drains them and runs callbacks on the engine (caller) thread.

decisions.mark: identifies the cancellation observer thread as existing to bridge an atomic into a plain int, because the C ABI boundary cannot carry an atomic
decisions.detail: QUOTE: The cancel pollers are the simplest case. Each one spins at 10 ms, reads an int or atomic, and sets an atomic `cancel_` flag. ... The C ABI passes only `int*`, so no `std::atomic` crosses the `.so` boundary. | WHY: The answer mentions cancel pollers and that the C ABI passes only `int*`, but never says the observer thread exists to bridge an atomic into a plain int because the ABI can't carry an atomic. It even describes the direction as reading an int and setting an atomic, which does not match the item. || QUOTE: "The C ABI passes only `int*`, so no `std::atomic` crosses the `.so` boundary." | WHY: The answer describes the cancel pollers (they read an int or atomic and set an atomic flag) and separately notes the C ABI passes only `int*`. It never says the observer thread exists to bridge an atomic into a plain int because of that ABI limit.
